newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH SAYS ECONOMY, NZ DLR, HIT Q1 MARGINS.
newsitem.headline: CHH SAYS ECONOMY, NZ DLR, HIT Q1 MARGINS.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd said on Thursday that a slowdown in the domestic economy, a high New Zealand dollar and cyclical lows in several of its businesses continued to place significant margin pressure across the group.
Chief executive John Faraci said the company had made significant improvements in operational performance, with volumes and sales up across most of its product lines.
In the forests business, volumes were up, largely offsetting price pressure.
"Overall, pricing in export markets, while improving, remains significantly below the levels of last year," Faraci told a news conference.
Aside from those factors the wood products group achieved steady growth with laminated veneer lumber volumes up 67 percent and timber up 30 percent on the prior year period.
The group's south east Australian operations, acquired in September last year, also contributed to group profitability and enabled it to achieve substantial volume growth there.

Weak pulp prices and a reduction in container and carton board margins continued to impact on the pulp and paper business. However, the tissue grop continued to perform well, with significant productivity gains made in Australia.
A soft New Zealand economy also placed further pressure on an already competitive environment for the packaging group.

"In light of this environment, volumes continue to grow and the newly acquired Australian plastics packaging business, Associated Plastics Indsutries, improves our capacity to supply our plastics packaging customers in Australia by gaining new business," Faraci said.
Pricing remained competitive for the building products and distribution group, with domestic building activity softening.
"The Australian businesses showed some improvements over recent results, benefiting from increased commercial and housing activity," Faraci said.
As expected, earnings from associated companies fell to NZ$24 million from $32 million. This reflected the impact of low pulp prices on its 30 percent owned associate, Copec.
CHH, which is just over half-owned by International Paper, earlier reported a first quarter net profit of NZ$49 million, down from $56 million a year earlier.

Faraci said he expected the first quarter to represent a low point for the company. He expected steady improvements throughout the rest of the financial year "but the market remains extremely competitive".
